Ana: Heads-up: planning a rate-limited backfill for user_flags to avoid locks during tomorrow's release window. Target window 02:00-04:00 UTC.
Devin: +1. What's the expected duration at ~1000 rows/s?
Ana: ~90m estimated, but we'll cap to 400 rows/s and watch queue lag. Should fit 2h with buffer.
Marta: Can we pin the migration runner image/version so accidental deploys don't change behavior mid-backfill?
Jeff: Yes — plan is to pin tag `migration-runner:v2024-11-3` and deploy a canary to staging first.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy by @ana at 2024-06-15T02:00Z for migration-runner:v2024-11-3 :robot_face:
Ana: Backfill command (run by migration-runner):
```
./backfill --table=user_flags --batch-size=400 --rate=400 --resume-token=$TOKEN
```
Devin: Suggest adding `--no-lock` style option and explicit `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` batching inside the job.
Ana: Yep, we'll use skip-locked + id-window batching. SQL sample:
```
BEGIN;
UPDATE user_flags SET processed = true
WHERE id IN (
  SELECT id FROM user_flags WHERE processed = false ORDER BY id LIMIT 400 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
);
COMMIT;
```
sre-oncall: Please add an alert if single shard sees > 120s per batch or replication lag > 30s. Also add kill-switch.
Ana: Kill-switch = posting `/cancel-backfill $RUN_ID` to ops channel which triggers deploybot rollback hook.
db-admin-bot: Warning: check index usage on user_flags.updated_at. If full table scan happens, pause and rollback.
Marta: Rollback plan: 1) Cancel backfill job, 2) revert migration-runner to previous tag `v2024-11-2`, 3) re-open emergency window and run a smaller staggered backfill.
Jeff: I'll own the revert and smoke tests. Who will monitor metrics (latency, cpu, replication)?
Devin: I'll watch DB metrics, @sre-oncall will watch app latency. We'll have a 15-min readiness gate for canary before proceeding to full rollout.
Ana: Thanks — I'll add these steps to the release notes and the deploy checklist. :thumbsup:
